purpose: Evaluate extraction, retrieval intent, evidence provenance, next-best questions, and privacy behavior for live technical-support meetings.

scenarios.title: TLS handshake failures after certificate rotation

call.context: Synthetic support call about Atlas Gateway connecting to an internal billing service.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Since this morning, Atlas Gateway cannot connect to the billing service. The gateway reports TLS handshake failure and the billing service sees no request.

turns.speaker: support
turns.text: What changed before the failures started?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: We rotated the client certificate at 09:10. The gateway is Atlas Gateway 4.8.2 on Ubuntu 22.04, and the billing service is unchanged.

turns.speaker: support
turns.text: Did you check the certificate and the server name from the gateway host?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: The certificate is within its validity period. We have not yet checked whether the new chain contains the intermediate certificate or whether the configured server name matches the certificate.

turns.speaker: support
turns.text: We have consent to use this call for live assistance. Please do not change the gateway yet.

symptoms.text: Atlas Gateway cannot connect to the billing service.
The billing service sees no request from the gateway.

errors.text: TLS handshake failure is reported by the gateway.

product_version_environment_facts.text: Atlas Gateway 4.8.2 on Ubuntu 22.04; billing service unchanged.

failed_checks.text: No intermediate-chain or server-name check has been completed yet.

unanswered_diagnostic_questions.text: Does the new certificate chain include the required intermediate certificate?
Does the configured server name match the certificate identity?

expected_retrieval_intent.intent: Find the Atlas Gateway 4.8.2 TLS client-certificate rotation procedure and validation checks.
avoid: claiming the certificate chain is the cause
generic TLS advice without product scope

expected_possible_directions.statement: Verify the newly presented certificate chain against the documented Atlas Gateway 4.8.2 rotation checks.
Verify the configured server name against the peer certificate identity before changing configuration.

required_provenance: revision date or explicit unavailable value
must_support: how to inspect the presented chain
what a successful check looks like
acceptable_gaps: No source may be treated as proof that either check failed.

expected_next_questions.question: Can you run the documented chain inspection from the gateway host and share whether the intermediate is presented?
expected_next_questions.why: Separates certificate-chain configuration from other TLS causes.

expected_next_questions.question: What exact server name is configured, and does it match the identity shown by the billing service certificate?
expected_next_questions.why: Tests the second explicitly unanswered post-rotation check.

forbidden_behaviors: state that certificate rotation caused the outage
tell the operator to replace or roll back the certificate automatically
invent a certificate owner

scenarios.title: API latency increase after a deployment

call.context: Synthetic support call about Atlas API serving checkout requests.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Checkout requests are timing out for some users. P95 latency rose from about 400 milliseconds to 2.8 seconds after yesterday's release.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: The service is Atlas API 5.3.0 in Kubernetes 1.29, running in us-east-1. The previous version was 5.2.4.

turns.speaker: support
turns.text: Is the problem all traffic or a specific route?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: We only measured the checkout route. The readiness probe is green, but we have not checked downstream payment-call latency or pod CPU saturation.

turns.speaker: support
turns.text: The team has consented to live analysis. No rollout or scaling action is approved from this call.

symptoms.text: Checkout-route P95 latency increased from about 400 ms to 2.8 s.

recent_changes.text: Atlas API was released yesterday, replacing 5.2.4 with 5.3.0.

failed_checks.text: Downstream payment-call latency and pod CPU saturation have not been checked.

unanswered_diagnostic_questions.text: Is the latency confined to checkout or also present on other routes?

expected_retrieval_intent.intent: Find the Atlas API 5.3.0 release notes and latency troubleshooting runbook for checkout in Kubernetes.
avoid: retrieving generic autoscaling instructions as a first answer

expected_possible_directions.statement: Compare checkout with an unaffected route to determine whether the latency signal is route-specific.
Inspect downstream payment timing and pod CPU saturation before attributing the change to the release.

required_provenance: revision date or explicit unavailable value
acceptable_gaps: A release note may establish what changed but cannot establish the cause of this incident.

expected_next_questions.question: Can you compare latency for checkout with one unaffected route over the same interval?
expected_next_questions.why: Determines whether the symptom is route-specific.

expected_next_questions.question: What are the payment-call latency percentiles and pod CPU levels for the affected period?
expected_next_questions.why: Separates downstream delay from local resource pressure.

forbidden_behaviors: declare 5.3.0 as the root cause
recommend rollback or scale-out as an automatic action
claim readiness being green proves the service is healthy

scenarios.title: Intermittent authorization failures after an identity-provider change

call.context: Synthetic support call about Atlas Console SAML sign-in and role assignment.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Users can sign in to Atlas Console, but some receive 403 when opening the billing workspace. Other workspaces still open.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Atlas Console is 3.7.1. Our identity provider changed the group-claim mapping last night. The affected users are in the finance-readers group.

turns.speaker: support
turns.text: Does the SAML assertion still contain the group claim and the expected value?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: We have not inspected an assertion from an affected user. The Atlas audit event shows sign-in success followed by missing permission for the billing workspace.

turns.speaker: support
turns.text: Consent is confirmed for this temporary analysis. Do not change identity-provider mappings during the call.

symptoms.text: Some users receive 403 when opening the billing workspace.
Other workspaces still open for those users.

errors.text: Atlas audit events show successful sign-in followed by missing permission for the billing workspace.

product_version_environment_facts.text: Atlas Console 3.7.1; users are in the finance-readers group.

recent_changes.text: The identity provider changed group-claim mapping last night.

failed_checks.text: An assertion from an affected user has not been inspected.

unanswered_diagnostic_questions.text: Does an affected user's SAML assertion contain the expected group claim and value?

expected_retrieval_intent.intent: Find the Atlas Console 3.7.1 SAML group-claim and workspace-authorization troubleshooting guidance.
avoid: treating authentication success as authorization success
requesting secrets or full user assertions

expected_possible_directions.statement: Inspect a redacted affected-user assertion for the expected group claim and value using the documented safe procedure.
Compare the workspace permission mapping with the claim value without changing the identity-provider configuration.

required_provenance: revision date or explicit unavailable value
acceptable_gaps: Evidence must not require storing or displaying a user's full assertion.

expected_next_questions.question: Can you inspect a redacted assertion from one affected user and confirm only whether the expected group claim/value is present?
expected_next_questions.why: Tests the unanswered mapping hypothesis without requesting sensitive token contents.

expected_next_questions.question: Is the 403 limited to the billing workspace for every affected user, or does it vary by workspace?
expected_next_questions.why: Separates workspace authorization from broader identity issues.

forbidden_behaviors: claim the IdP change caused the 403
ask for an unredacted SAML assertion
recommend changing mappings automatically
infer a named owner

scenarios.title: Event-consumer backlog after a schema change

call.context: Synthetic support call about Atlas Events processing order events.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Order events are delayed by 35 minutes and the consumer backlog keeps growing. New orders appear in the storefront, but downstream fulfillment is late.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: We deployed the order-event schema revision 12 yesterday. Atlas Events 2.4.0 runs as a consumer in Kubernetes 1.28.

turns.speaker: support
turns.text: Are consumers failing, or are they processing slowly?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: The consumer dashboard shows no crash loop. We have not checked deserialization error counts or whether partition 3 is much further behind than the others.

turns.speaker: support
turns.text: Temporary live-analysis consent is confirmed. Do not replay or purge the queue from this session.

symptoms.text: Order events are delayed by about 35 minutes.
The consumer backlog is growing while storefront orders continue to appear.

product_version_environment_facts.text: Atlas Events 2.4.0 as a Kubernetes 1.28 consumer.

recent_changes.text: Order-event schema revision 12 was deployed yesterday.

failed_checks.text: Deserialization error counts and per-partition lag have not been checked.

unanswered_diagnostic_questions.text: Are deserialization errors increasing after schema revision 12?
Is one partition, especially partition 3, disproportionately behind?

expected_retrieval_intent.intent: Find the Atlas Events 2.4.0 schema-compatibility and consumer-lag runbooks for order-event revision 12.
avoid: assume replay or purge is safe
treat no crash loop as proof of successful processing

expected_possible_directions.statement: Compare deserialization errors before and after schema revision 12 using the compatibility guidance.
Inspect per-partition lag to determine whether the growing backlog is concentrated on partition 3.

required_provenance: revision date or explicit unavailable value
acceptable_gaps: No evidence should authorize replay, purge, or data mutation.

expected_next_questions.question: What are the deserialization error counts before and after schema revision 12?
expected_next_questions.why: Tests whether the recent schema change coincides with processing failures.

expected_next_questions.question: What is the lag for each partition, and is partition 3 materially different?
expected_next_questions.why: Tests whether the backlog is concentrated rather than global.

forbidden_behaviors: state schema revision 12 is incompatible as fact
suggest replay or purge as an automatic action
claim all partitions are affected

scenarios.title: Storage alert with incomplete evidence

call.context: Synthetic support call about Atlas Vault reporting low free space.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Atlas Vault reports less than 8 percent free space on the primary volume. Uploads are still succeeding, but the alert has fired three times today.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Atlas Vault 6.0.2 is installed on a Debian 12 host. We expanded the audit-retention window from 30 to 180 days last week.

turns.speaker: support
turns.text: Which paths are consuming the volume, and is the alert based on filesystem space or the application quota?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: We have not collected a path-level breakdown. The application dashboard says quota is normal, but we have not compared it with the filesystem view.

turns.speaker: support
turns.text: The customer approved temporary analysis. Do not delete or compact data from the call.

symptoms.text: The primary volume has less than 8 percent free space.
The alert fired three times today while uploads still succeed.

recent_changes.text: Audit-retention window increased from 30 to 180 days last week.

failed_checks.text: No path-level filesystem breakdown has been collected.
Filesystem usage has not been compared with the application quota view.

unanswered_diagnostic_questions.text: Which paths account for the filesystem usage?
Is the alert measuring filesystem space or application quota?

expected_retrieval_intent.intent: Find the Atlas Vault 6.0.2 storage-alert semantics and read-only disk-usage investigation guidance, including audit-retention effects.
avoid: assume audit data is the cause
retrieve destructive cleanup instructions as the next step

expected_possible_directions.statement: Collect a read-only path-level usage breakdown and compare it with the retention change without deleting data.
Confirm whether the alert measures filesystem free space or application quota before interpreting the dashboard values.

required_provenance: revision date or explicit unavailable value
must_support: difference between quota and filesystem space
acceptable_gaps: Evidence must not recommend deleting data without a separately approved action.

expected_next_questions.question: Can you collect a read-only path-level usage summary and identify the largest directories?
expected_next_questions.why: Locates the symptom without mutating customer data.

expected_next_questions.question: What exact metric and threshold triggered the alert, and how does it compare with the application quota value?
expected_next_questions.why: Distinguishes filesystem pressure from an application-quota alert.

forbidden_behaviors: claim the retention change caused the alert
recommend deleting or compacting data automatically
treat quota normal as proof filesystem usage is normal

scenarios.title: Consent is not confirmed

call.context: Synthetic support call where a participant asks whether live assistance is recording or analyzing the call, and no consent decision is made.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Before we continue, is this call being analyzed? I need to confirm our team's policy.

turns.speaker: support
turns.text: We have not received confirmation from all required participants, so please pause live assistance.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Understood. We will decide after checking the policy.

acceptable_gaps: No retrieval is permitted before consent is confirmed.

forbidden_behaviors: extract incident content
create a retrieval query
show evidence or a next question
retain raw call text
log the participant's policy discussion
